paper.title: Spillover Effects of Early-Life Medical Interventions
paper.journal: The Review of Economics and Statistics
paper.code_data_availability: No data or code availability statement appears in the paper and no Statistics Denmark project number is given. …

registers.role: sample frame, treatment (birth weight), linkage to parents and siblings, and covariates

registers.name_in_paper: other register data (providing information on both parents and children regarding demographic characteristics, labor market outcomes, health outcomes, and academic achievement)
registers.role: outcomes (hospitalizations and ER visits, disability diagnoses, ninth-grade test scores, enrollment, days worked, employment, annual gross income) and covariates (parental age, education, marital and immigrant status)

linkages: Using parental identifiers from the Birth Register, children are linked to their parents and siblings and parity is determined.
Siblings are defined as children born to the same mother from different pregnancies; each sibling-focal child pair is an independent observation.

If the mother is married to a man at the time of birth the husband is automatically registered as the biological father; parental identifiers for fathers are missing for forty focal children in the FC sample.

sample.universe: The universe of births in Denmark recorded in the Birth Register (from 1970); the analysis starts from focal children born 1982-1993.
sample.unit_of_observation: focal child (and, for the sibling analyses, the sibling-focal child pair); for parents, the mother or father of a focal child
selection_rules: Select focal children born between 1982 and 1993.
Exclude observations for which either birth weight or gestational age is missing.
Restrict the sample to birth weight within 1,300 to 1,700 grams (a 200 g bandwidth around the 1,500 g VLBW cutoff).
Restrict to the 3,677 focal children with siblings.

Focus exclusively on the 2,156 focal children with gestational age of at least 32 weeks (the FC sample); the 1,521 focal children with gestational age below 32 weeks are used only in a falsification check.
Siblings: children born to the same mother from a different pregnancy, older and younger, giving 3,311 siblings of focal children with gestational age of at least 32 weeks (the sibling sample).
Academic outcomes are restricted to siblings old enough to be observed: cohorts born 1986-1997 for test scores and 1970-1993 for enrollment.
sample.period: focal children born 1982-1993; ninth-grade test scores available 2001-2010; outcomes followed up to fifteen years after the birth of the focal child
sample.n_observations: 2,156 focal children; 3,311 sibling-focal child pairs; 2,156 mothers; 2,116 fathers (estimation samples vary by outcome, from 669 to 3,311)
sample.n_individuals: 2,156 focal children with gestational age of at least 32 weeks (out of 3,677 focal children with siblings)

construction_notes: Each summary index is built in two steps: every component variable is standardized by the birth cohort of the focal child to mean 0 and standard deviation 1, the standardized components are averaged, and the index is restandardized at the level of the birth cohort of the focal child (appendix table A1 lists the components).
Birth weight is recorded in 250 gram intervals between 1973 and 1978, in 10 gram intervals between 1979 and 1990, and at the gram level since 1991.
Gestational age was added to the Birth Register beginning in 1982.

Bandwidth: 200 grams, chosen in preference to the rule-of-thumb optimal bandwidths of Calonico, Cattaneo and Titiunik (2014), which range from 118 to 251 grams with an average of 189 grams (appendix table A2).
All specifications control for indicators for heaping at multiples of 50 grams (Barreca et al., 2011).

Inference: robust confidence intervals centred on bias-corrected estimates using the standard errors from a specification with a second-degree polynomial in the running variable (Calonico et al., 2014, 2019); sharpened false-discovery-rate q-values following Anderson (2008).

Maternal education is missing for 315 observations corresponding to 154 mothers; these are replaced with the median number of years of education by birth cohort and an indicator for imputed maternal education is included.
Antidepressant use can only be constructed from focal child age 2 because the prescription drug register begins recording data in 1995.
Income indices use the log real annual gross income.
Test scores are missing for approximately 20% of the eligible cohorts in the sibling sample because children can be exempted from taking the test.

Figures plot binned means in 40 g bins with a first-degree polynomial estimated separately on either side of the cutoff; observations with birth weight of exactly 1,500 g are excluded from the figures.

links.pointer_quote: Using population-level data from Denmark, we first replicate the finding in the previous literature that VLBW children are significantly less likely to die within the first year of life relative to newborns with slightly higher birth weight.

claims.statement: VLBW classification of the focal child lowers the focal child's mortality summary index (28-day and 1-year mortality).

treatment.label: VLBW classification (very low birth weight: focal child birth weight below 1,500 grams)

register_source.value: Birth Register: birth weight of the focal child (the paper names no DST variable name)

definition.value: VLBWj, an indicator for focal child j having birth weight below 1,500 grams -- the threshold at which Danish medical guidelines prescribe additional early-life medical treatment. The estimated object is the jump in the outcome at the threshold in a local-linear RD with a 200 g bandwidth (1,300-1,700 g) and a triangular kernel; the paper observes the classification, not the treatments actually received.

timing.value: measured at the birth of the focal child (births 1982-1993)

register_source.value: other register data linked to the Birth Register; the paper names no specific register or variable for this outcome

definition.value: Mortality summary index combining two previously studied short-term outcomes, 28-day and 1-year mortality. Built in two steps: each component is standardized by the birth cohort of the focal child, the standardized components are averaged, and the index is restandardized at the level of the birth cohort of the focal child (appendix table A1 lists the components).

timing.value: 28 days and 1 year after the birth of the focal child

units.value: standard deviations of the summary index (each index is standardized to mean 0 and standard deviation 1 at the level of the birth cohort of the focal child)

magnitude.interpretation: The paper calls this 'mortality is 0.508 standard deviation lower'; the corresponding components in appendix table A6 are 4.1 and 5.4 percentage point reductions in 28-day and 1-year mortality against means of 6.2% and 7.7%.

estimand.target_population: focal children born in Denmark 1982-1993 with birth weight at the 1,500 g VLBW cutoff and gestational age of at least 32 weeks
estimand.time_horizon: short term: 28-day and 1-year mortality
estimand.formal_query: lim(bw -> 1500-) E[Y | bw] - lim(bw -> 1500+) E[Y | bw]: the intention-to-treat effect of VLBW classification of the focal child at the 1,500 g cutoff, for focal children born in Denmark 1982-1993 with birth weight at the 1,500 g VLBW cutoff and gestational age of at least 32 weeks

population.description: Focal children born in Denmark between 1982 and 1993 with non-missing birth weight and gestational age, birth weight within 1,300-1,700 g, at least one sibling and gestational age of at least 32 weeks (the FC sample, N = 2,156).
population.period: focal children born 1982-1993; outcomes followed up to fifteen years after the birth of the focal child
subgroups_defined: families in which the focal child survives the first year of life
population.selection: Focal children are conditioned on having a recorded birth weight and gestational age, birth weight within 200 g of the 1,500 g cutoff, at least one sibling born within the sample period, and gestational age of at least 32 weeks; the 1,521 focal children with gestational age below 32 weeks are used only in a falsification check.

identification.source_of_variation: The 1,500 gram very low birth weight threshold in Danish medical guidelines, which prescribe additional early-life medical treatment to newborns below it; births in Denmark 1982-1993 with gestational age of at least 32 weeks, for whom the 32-week gestational-age guideline does not already bind.

key_assumptions.assumption: Individuals do not have precise control over the assignment variable: mothers cannot precisely predict the birth weight of their children, so variation in birth weight near the VLBW cutoff is as good as random.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Frequency of births by 10 g birth weight bin in the FC/parent and sibling samples (appendix figure A1) and a local-linear regression with the number of births per bin as the dependent variable (McCrary, 2008): no evidence of a discontinuity in the frequency of births at the cutoff.

key_assumptions.assumption: Predetermined characteristics of focal children, their parents and their siblings are continuous at the VLBW cutoff, so that observations just below the cutoff are comparable to those just above it.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Table 1: the baseline model estimated with each covariate as the dependent variable; few marginally significant discontinuities and none survives the adjustment for multiple inference (lowest q-value 0.5).

implies_edges.from: predetermined child, parental and sibling characteristics
implies_edges.to: VLBW classification (focal child birth weight below 1,500 g)

key_assumptions.assumption: Nothing other than the additional medical treatments prescribed for VLBW newborns changes discontinuously at 1,500 grams; the discontinuity in the outcome is therefore attributable to those treatments.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Two falsification checks: the baseline model in the sample with gestational age below 32 weeks, where eligibility for additional treatment does not change at 1,500 g (appendix table A4, column 8), and placebo cutoffs from 1,300 to 3,100 grams (appendix figure A9).

implies_edges.from: other determinants of outcomes that change discontinuously at 1,500 g
implies_edges.to: focal child mortality summary index (28-day and 1-year mortality)

key_assumptions.assumption: The receipt of additional medical treatments around the VLBW cutoff does not change fertility, so family composition is not endogenous to treatment.
key_assumptions.supported_by: No discontinuity at the cutoff in the probability of having a younger sibling, the number of younger siblings or the birth spacing between focal children and younger siblings (table 1).

implies_edges.from: VLBW classification (focal child birth weight below 1,500 g)
implies_edges.to: subsequent fertility and family composition

key_assumptions.assumption: A first-degree polynomial in birth weight, allowed to differ on each side of the cutoff and weighted by a triangular kernel on a 200 g bandwidth, approximates the conditional mean of the outcome well enough that the estimated jump is the treatment effect at the cutoff.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stability of the estimates across bandwidths from 100 to 300 g (appendix figure A5), a second-degree polynomial and a rectangular kernel (appendix table A4).

threats_discussed: Physicians systematically misreporting birth weight, especially in the presence of financial incentives for manipulation
Manipulation of the running variable (precise control over birth weight)
Reporting heaps at multiples of 50 and 100 grams
Discretization bias from birth weight being recorded in 10 gram intervals for most of the sample period
Multiple inference across many outcomes, domains and family members
Differential survival of focal children at the cutoff (selection into the samples observed after infancy)
Correlated health shocks within the family that would make siblings themselves more likely to receive early-life medical treatments
Siblings being exempted from the ninth-grade test (test scores missing for about 20% of eligible cohorts in the sibling sample)
Delayed school entry / differential age at which the ninth-grade test is taken
Correlation in the error terms between pairs of siblings from the same household
Fertility responses to the birth of a VLBW focal child

prior_findings_compared.citation: Almond et al. (2010); Bharadwaj et al. (2013)
prior_findings_compared.as_stated: we first replicate the finding in the previous literature that VLBW children are significantly less likely to die within the first year of life relative to newborns with slightly higher birth weight.

falsification.condition: The authors state two falsification conditions: in the sample of focal children with gestational age below 32 weeks, where eligibility for additional medical treatment does not change at 1,500 g, 'any discontinuity in their outcomes or in the outcomes of their family members would suggest a violation of the key identification assumptions underlying the RD design'; and, if the gains are driven by the medical treatments, 'then we should not observe systematic discontinuities in the outcomes at other potential cutoffs'.

key_assumptions.assumption: Individuals do not have precise control over the assignment variable: mothers cannot precisely predict the birth weight of their children, so variation in birth weight near the VLBW cutoff is as good as random.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Frequency of births by 10 g birth weight bin in the FC/parent and sibling samples (appendix figure A1) and a local-linear regression with the number of births per bin as the dependent variable (McCrary, 2008): no evidence of a discontinuity in the frequency of births at the cutoff.

key_assumptions.assumption: Predetermined characteristics of focal children, their parents and their siblings are continuous at the VLBW cutoff, so that observations just below the cutoff are comparable to those just above it.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Table 1: the baseline model estimated with each covariate as the dependent variable; few marginally significant discontinuities and none survives the adjustment for multiple inference (lowest q-value 0.5).

falsification.condition: The authors state two falsification conditions: in the sample of focal children with gestational age below 32 weeks, where eligibility for additional medical treatment does not change at 1,500 g, 'any discontinuity in their outcomes or in the outcomes of their family members would suggest a violation of the key identification assumptions underlying the RD design'; and, if the gains are driven by the medical treatments, 'then we should not observe systematic discontinuities in the outcomes at other potential cutoffs'.

anchor_quote.text: We also find that focal children just below the VLBW cutoff have on average 0.314 standard deviation higher test scores in the ninth grade, but they are not significantly more likely to be enrolled beyond compulsory education.

claims.statement: VLBW classification of the focal child has no detectable effect on the index of enrollment beyond compulsory education of siblings.

treatment.label: VLBW classification (very low birth weight: focal child birth weight below 1,500 grams)

register_source.value: Birth Register: birth weight of the focal child (the paper names no DST variable name)

definition.value: VLBWj, an indicator for focal child j having birth weight below 1,500 grams -- the threshold at which Danish medical guidelines prescribe additional early-life medical treatment. The estimated object is the jump in the outcome at the threshold in a local-linear RD with a 200 g bandwidth (1,300-1,700 g) and a triangular kernel; the paper observes the classification, not the treatments actually received.

timing.value: measured at the birth of the focal child (births 1982-1993)

outcome.label: Higher education (index of enrollment beyond compulsory education, siblings)

register_source.value: other register data linked to the Birth Register; the paper names no specific register or variable for this outcome

definition.value: Index of enrollment beyond compulsory education (nine years during the sample period) using indicators for enrollment in high school or vocational school at age 18, enrollment in an academic track at age 18, enrollment in higher education at age 24, and enrollment in a university at age 24. Built in two steps: each component is standardized by the birth cohort of the focal child, the standardized components are averaged, and the index is restandardized at the level of the birth cohort of the focal child (appendix table A1 lists the components).

timing.value: ages 18 and 24

units.value: standard deviations of the summary index (each index is standardized to mean 0 and standard deviation 1 at the level of the birth cohort of the focal child)

identification.source_of_variation: The 1,500 gram very low birth weight threshold in Danish medical guidelines, which prescribe additional early-life medical treatment to newborns below it; births in Denmark 1982-1993 with gestational age of at least 32 weeks, for whom the 32-week gestational-age guideline does not already bind.

key_assumptions.assumption: Individuals do not have precise control over the assignment variable: mothers cannot precisely predict the birth weight of their children, so variation in birth weight near the VLBW cutoff is as good as random.

key_assumptions.assumption: Predetermined characteristics of focal children, their parents and their siblings are continuous at the VLBW cutoff, so that observations just below the cutoff are comparable to those just above it.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Table 1: the baseline model estimated with each covariate as the dependent variable; few marginally significant discontinuities and none survives the adjustment for multiple inference (lowest q-value 0.5).

value.claimed_domain: developed countries with a particularly generous social safety net
boundary_conditions: Denmark has one of the most generous social safety nets in the world, including 52 weeks of parental leave, generous cash payments to families with children, heavily subsidized child care, and free and universal health care

falsification.condition: The authors state two falsification conditions: in the sample of focal children with gestational age below 32 weeks, where eligibility for additional medical treatment does not change at 1,500 g, 'any discontinuity in their outcomes or in the outcomes of their family members would suggest a violation of the key identification assumptions underlying the RD design'; and, if the gains are driven by the medical treatments, 'then we should not observe systematic discontinuities in the outcomes at other potential cutoffs'.

claims.statement: VLBW classification of the focal child has no effect that survives multiple-inference adjustment on the father's long-term employment summary index.

treatment.label: VLBW classification (very low birth weight: focal child birth weight below 1,500 grams)

register_source.value: Birth Register: birth weight of the focal child (the paper names no DST variable name)

definition.value: VLBWj, an indicator for focal child j having birth weight below 1,500 grams -- the threshold at which Danish medical guidelines prescribe additional early-life medical treatment. The estimated object is the jump in the outcome at the threshold in a local-linear RD with a 200 g bandwidth (1,300-1,700 g) and a triangular kernel; the paper observes the classification, not the treatments actually received.

timing.value: measured at the birth of the focal child (births 1982-1993)

outcome.label: Labor market outcomes (long-term employment summary index, father)

register_source.value: other register data linked to the Birth Register; the paper names no specific register or variable for this outcome

definition.value: Long-term employment index based on the number of days worked and indicators for being employed in each calendar year when the focal child is 6 to 15 years old. Built in two steps: each component is standardized by the birth cohort of the focal child, the standardized components are averaged, and the index is restandardized at the level of the birth cohort of the focal child (appendix table A1 lists the components).

timing.value: each calendar year when the focal child is 6 to 15 years old

units.value: standard deviations of the summary index (each index is standardized to mean 0 and standard deviation 1 at the level of the birth cohort of the focal child)

estimand.time_horizon: long term: when the focal child is 6 to 15 years old

population.description: Fathers of the focal children in the FC sample; paternal identifiers are missing for forty of the focal children.
population.period: focal children born 1982-1993; outcomes followed up to fifteen years after the birth of the focal child
subgroups_defined: families in which the focal child survives the first year of life
population.selection: Focal children are conditioned on having a recorded birth weight and gestational age, birth weight within 200 g of the 1,500 g cutoff, at least one sibling born within the sample period, and gestational age of at least 32 weeks; the 1,521 focal children with gestational age below 32 weeks are used only in a falsification check. identification.source_of_variation: The 1,500 gram very low birth weight threshold in Danish medical guidelines, which prescribe additional early-life medical treatment to newborns below it; births in Denmark 1982-1993 with gestational age of at least 32 weeks, for whom the 32-week gestational-age guideline does not already bind.

key_assumptions.assumption: Individuals do not have precise control over the assignment variable: mothers cannot precisely predict the birth weight of their children, so variation in birth weight near the VLBW cutoff is as good as random.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Frequency of births by 10 g birth weight bin in the FC/parent and sibling samples (appendix figure A1) and a local-linear regression with the number of births per bin as the dependent variable (McCrary, 2008): no evidence of a discontinuity in the frequency of births at the cutoff.

key_assumptions.assumption: Predetermined characteristics of focal children, their parents and their siblings are continuous at the VLBW cutoff, so that observations just below the cutoff are comparable to those just above it.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Table 1: the baseline model estimated with each covariate as the dependent variable; few marginally significant discontinuities and none survives the adjustment for multiple inference (lowest q-value 0.5).

implies_edges.from: predetermined child, parental and sibling characteristics
implies_edges.to: VLBW classification (focal child birth weight below 1,500 g)

key_assumptions.assumption: Nothing other than the additional medical treatments prescribed for VLBW newborns changes discontinuously at 1,500 grams; the discontinuity in the outcome is therefore attributable to those treatments.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Two falsification checks: the baseline model in the sample with gestational age below 32 weeks, where eligibility for additional treatment does not change at 1,500 g (appendix table A4, column 8), and placebo cutoffs from 1,300 to 3,100 grams (appendix figure A9).

implies_edges.from: other determinants of outcomes that change discontinuously at 1,500 g
implies_edges.to: father long-term employment index (days worked and employment, focal child aged 6-15)

key_assumptions.assumption: The receipt of additional medical treatments around the VLBW cutoff does not change fertility, so family composition is not endogenous to treatment.
key_assumptions.supported_by: No discontinuity at the cutoff in the probability of having a younger sibling, the number of younger siblings or the birth spacing between focal children and younger siblings (table 1).

implies_edges.from: VLBW classification (focal child birth weight below 1,500 g)
implies_edges.to: subsequent fertility and family composition

key_assumptions.assumption: A first-degree polynomial in birth weight, allowed to differ on each side of the cutoff and weighted by a triangular kernel on a 200 g bandwidth, approximates the conditional mean of the outcome well enough that the estimated jump is the treatment effect at the cutoff.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stability of the estimates across bandwidths from 100 to 300 g (appendix figure A5), a second-degree polynomial and a rectangular kernel (appendix table A4).

The point estimate recorded here is the conventional estimate (bias-corrected estimate: [0.252]).

The table marks this estimate with one asterisk (significant at 10% based on robust confidence intervals centred on the bias-corrected estimate). It is not significant at 5% and the paper's own reading is null -- 'we generally do not find significant discontinuities ... in the measures of family resources' and the marginally significant gains 'do not survive the adjustment for multiple inference'. statistically_significant is therefore recorded as false. Sharpened q-value: {0.239}.

boundary_conditions: Denmark has one of the most generous social safety nets in the world, including 52 weeks of parental leave, generous cash payments to families with children, heavily subsidized child care, and free and universal health care

key_assumptions.assumption: Nothing other than the additional medical treatments prescribed for VLBW newborns changes discontinuously at 1,500 grams; the discontinuity in the outcome is therefore attributable to those treatments.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Two falsification checks: the baseline model in the sample with gestational age below 32 weeks, where eligibility for additional treatment does not change at 1,500 g (appendix table A4, column 8), and placebo cutoffs from 1,300 to 3,100 grams (appendix figure A9).

implies_edges.to: sibling ninth-grade language test score

key_assumptions.assumption: The receipt of additional medical treatments around the VLBW cutoff does not change fertility, so family composition is not endogenous to treatment.
key_assumptions.supported_by: No discontinuity at the cutoff in the probability of having a younger sibling, the number of younger siblings or the birth spacing between focal children and younger siblings (table 1).

implies_edges.from: VLBW classification (focal child birth weight below 1,500 g)
implies_edges.to: subsequent fertility and family composition

key_assumptions.assumption: A first-degree polynomial in birth weight, allowed to differ on each side of the cutoff and weighted by a triangular kernel on a 200 g bandwidth, approximates the conditional mean of the outcome well enough that the estimated jump is the treatment effect at the cutoff.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stability of the estimates across bandwidths from 100 to 300 g (appendix figure A5), a second-degree polynomial and a rectangular kernel (appendix table A4).

key_assumptions.assumption: Each sibling-focal child pair can be treated as an independent observation, despite potential correlation in the error terms between pairs of siblings from the same household.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Results reported as qualitatively similar when the standard errors are clustered at the mother level (available on request).

key_assumptions.assumption: Selection into taking the ninth-grade test is unrelated to the VLBW classification of the focal child (test scores are missing for about 20% of the eligible cohorts in the sibling sample because children can be exempted).
key_assumptions.supported_by: No discontinuity at the cutoff in the probability that a sibling takes the language test (0.029) or the math test (0.048), nor in the age at which the test is taken (-0.139); and the age at which focal children take the test is smooth (-0.033).

treatment.label: VLBW classification (very low birth weight: focal child birth weight below 1,500 grams)

key_assumptions.supported_by: Table 1: the baseline model estimated with each covariate as the dependent variable; few marginally significant discontinuities and none survives the adjustment for multiple inference (lowest q-value 0.5).

treatment.label: VLBW classification (very low birth weight: focal child birth weight below 1,500 grams)

definition.value: VLBWj, an indicator for focal child j having birth weight below 1,500 grams -- the threshold at which Danish medical guidelines prescribe additional early-life medical treatment. population.description: Siblings (children born to the same mother from a different pregnancy, older and younger) of the focal children in the FC sample (the sibling sample, N = 3,311 sibling-focal child pairs).

identification.source_of_variation: The 1,500 gram very low birth weight threshold in Danish medical guidelines, which prescribe additional early-life medical treatment to newborns below it; births in Denmark 1982-1993 with gestational age of at least 32 weeks, for whom the 32-week gestational-age guideline does not already bind.

key_assumptions.assumption: Individuals do not have precise control over the assignment variable: mothers cannot precisely predict the birth weight of their children, so variation in birth weight near the VLBW cutoff is as good as random.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Frequency of births by 10 g birth weight bin in the FC/parent and sibling samples (appendix figure A1) and a local-linear regression with the number of births per bin as the dependent variable (McCrary, 2008): no evidence of a discontinuity in the frequency of births at the cutoff.

key_assumptions.assumption: Predetermined characteristics of focal children, their parents and their siblings are continuous at the VLBW cutoff, so that observations just below the cutoff are comparable to those just above it.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Table 1: the baseline model estimated with each covariate as the dependent variable; few marginally significant discontinuities and none survives the adjustment for multiple inference (lowest q-value 0.5).

implies_edges.to: subsequent fertility and family composition

key_assumptions.assumption: A first-degree polynomial in birth weight, allowed to differ on each side of the cutoff and weighted by a triangular kernel on a 200 g bandwidth, approximates the conditional mean of the outcome well enough that the estimated jump is the treatment effect at the cutoff.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stability of the estimates across bandwidths from 100 to 300 g (appendix figure A5), a second-degree polynomial and a rectangular kernel (appendix table A4).

key_assumptions.assumption: Each sibling-focal child pair can be treated as an independent observation, despite potential correlation in the error terms between pairs of siblings from the same household.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Results reported as qualitatively similar when the standard errors are clustered at the mother level (available on request).

key_assumptions.assumption: Individuals do not have precise control over the assignment variable: mothers cannot precisely predict the birth weight of their children, so variation in birth weight near the VLBW cutoff is as good as random.

key_assumptions.assumption: Predetermined characteristics of focal children, their parents and their siblings are continuous at the VLBW cutoff, so that observations just below the cutoff are comparable to those just above it.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Table 1: the baseline model estimated with each covariate as the dependent variable; few marginally significant discontinuities and none survives the adjustment for multiple inference (lowest q-value 0.5).

population.selection: Focal children are conditioned on having a recorded birth weight and gestational age, birth weight within 200 g of the 1,500 g cutoff, at least one sibling born within the sample period, and gestational age of at least 32 weeks; the 1,521 focal children with gestational age below 32 weeks are used only in a falsification check.

identification.source_of_variation: The 1,500 gram very low birth weight threshold in Danish medical guidelines, which prescribe additional early-life medical treatment to newborns below it; births in Denmark 1982-1993 with gestational age of at least 32 weeks, for whom the 32-week gestational-age guideline does not already bind.

key_assumptions.assumption: Individuals do not have precise control over the assignment variable: mothers cannot precisely predict the birth weight of their children, so variation in birth weight near the VLBW cutoff is as good as random.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Frequency of births by 10 g birth weight bin in the FC/parent and sibling samples (appendix figure A1) and a local-linear regression with the number of births per bin as the dependent variable (McCrary, 2008): no evidence of a discontinuity in the frequency of births at the cutoff.

key_assumptions.assumption: A first-degree polynomial in birth weight, allowed to differ on each side of the cutoff and weighted by a triangular kernel on a 200 g bandwidth, approximates the conditional mean of the outcome well enough that the estimated jump is the treatment effect at the cutoff.
key_assumptions.supported_by: Stability of the estimates across bandwidths from 100 to 300 g (appendix figure A5), a second-degree polynomial and a rectangular kernel (appendix table A4).
